records.reference: CONCORD RETURNED TO ITS PLACE AMIDST THE TENTS
records.text: Concord returned to its place amidst the tents.

records.reference: IF A ROCK OR A RIVULET OR A BIT OF EARTH HARDER THAN COMMON SEVERED THE LINKS OF THE CLEW THEY FOLLOWED THE TRUE EYE OF THE SCOUT RECOVERED THEM AT A DISTANCE AND SELDOM RENDERED THE DELAY OF A SINGLE MOMENT NECESSARY
records.text: If a rock, or a rivulet, or a bit of earth harder than common, severed the links of the clew they followed, the true eye of the scout recovered them at a distance, and seldom rendered the delay of a single moment necessary.

records.reference: THIS WAS AT THE MARCH ELECTION EIGHTEEN FIFTY FIVE
records.text: This was at the March election, eighteen fifty five.

records.reference: I DON'T ALWAYS SUCCEED FOR SOMETIMES WHEN I'M TEACHING OR SEWING I WOULD RATHER BE READING OR WRITING BUT I TRY TO DENY MYSELF AND MY FATHER'S APPROBATION AMPLY REWARDED ME FOR THE PRIVATION
records.text: I don't always succeed, for sometimes when I'm teaching or sewing I would rather be reading or writing but I try to deny myself, and my father's approbation amply rewarded me for the privation.

records.reference: LISTEN THEN SOCRATES TO A TALE OF SOLON'S WHO BEING THE FRIEND OF DROPIDAS MY GREAT GRANDFATHER TOLD IT TO MY GRANDFATHER CRITIAS AND HE TOLD ME
records.text: Listen, then, Socrates, to a tale of Solons, who, being the friend of Dropidas, my great grandfather, told it to my grandfather Critias, and he told me.

records.reference: WE ARE OF COURSE IN FACT ABLE TO JUDGE WHEN WE RECOGNIZE AN OBJECT THAT WE HAVE SEEN IT BEFORE BUT THIS JUDGMENT IS SOMETHING OVER AND ABOVE RECOGNITION IN THIS FIRST SENSE AND MAY VERY PROBABLY BE IMPOSSIBLE TO ANIMALS THAT NEVERTHELESS HAVE THE EXPERIENCE OF RECOGNITION IN THIS FIRST SENSE OF THE WORD
records.text: We are, of course, in fact able to judge, when we recognize an object, that we have seen it before but this judgment is something over and above recognition in this first sense, and may very probably be impossible to animals that nevertheless have the experience of recognition in this first sense of the word.

records.reference: THE LAGOON HAD BEEN LEVEL WITH THE DYKES A WEEK AGO AND NOW
records.text: The lagoon had been level with the dikes a week ago, and now,

records.reference: OH IT IS BETTER TO LIVE ON THE SEA AND LET OTHER MEN RAISE YOUR CROPS AND COOK YOUR MEALS
records.text: Oh, it is better to live on the sea and let other men raise your crops and cook your meals.

records.reference: DO YOU SUPPOSE THAT GOD FOR THE SAKE OF A FEW LUTHERAN HERETICS WOULD DISOWN HIS ENTIRE CHURCH
records.text: Do you suppose that God, for the sake of a few Lutheran heretics, would disown his entire church?

records.reference: WHAT SHE WANTED FROM US WAS NEITHER OUR FLOWERS NOR OUR FRANCS BUT JUST OUR YOUTH
records.text: What she wanted from us was neither our flowers nor our francs, but just our youth.

records.reference: HESTER COULD ONLY ACCOUNT FOR THE CHILD'S CHARACTER AND EVEN THEN MOST VAGUELY AND IMPERFECTLY BY RECALLING WHAT SHE HERSELF HAD BEEN DURING THAT MOMENTOUS PERIOD WHILE PEARL WAS IMBIBING HER SOUL FROM THE SPIRITUAL WORLD AND HER BODILY FRAME FROM ITS MATERIAL OF EARTH
records.text: Hester could only account for the child's character, and even then most vaguely and imperfectly, by recalling what she herself had been, during that momentous period, while Pearl was imbibing her soul from the spiritual world, and her bodily frame from its material of earth

records.reference: AND THE MEN OF ISRAEL ANSWERED THE MEN OF JUDAH AND SAID WE HAVE TEN PARTS IN THE KING AND WE HAVE ALSO MORE RIGHT IN DAVID THAN YE WHY THEN DID YE DESPISE US THAT OUR ADVICE SHOULD NOT BE FIRST HAD IN BRINGING BACK OUR KING
records.text: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye. Why, then, did ye despise us that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king?

records.reference: WHAT'S THE MEANING OF THIS THOUGHT THE TREE
records.text: What's the meaning of this? thought the Tree.

records.reference: I RESIDE IN THE MARAIS RUE DE DOUZE PORTES
records.text: I reside in the Marie Grue de Duxport.

records.reference: HE SOON FORESAW THAT STILL GREATER ECONOMY WOULD BE NECESSARY FOR COMMERCIAL SUCCESS NOT ALONE FOR THE LARGER TERRITORY OPENING BUT FOR THE COMPACT DISTRICTS OF LARGE CITIES
records.text: He soon foresaw that still greater economy would be necessary for commercial success not alone for the larger territory opening, but for the compact district of large cities.

records.reference: I WAS IN SUCH A HURRY TO COME TO YOU YOU LEFT YOUR DOOR OPEN
records.text: I was in such a hurry to come to you. You left your door open?

records.reference: THE MODEST FELLOW WOULD HAVE LIKED FAME THRUST UPON HIM FOR SOME WORTHY ACHIEVEMENT IT MIGHT BE FOR A BOOK OR FOR THE SKILLFUL MANAGEMENT OF SOME GREAT NEWSPAPER OR FOR SOME DARING EXPEDITION LIKE THAT OF LIEUTENANT STRAIN OR DOCTOR KANE
records.text: The modest fellow would have liked fame thrust upon him for some worthy achievement it might be for a book, or for the skilful management of some great newspaper, or for some daring expedition like that of Lieutenant Strayne or doctor Kane.

records.reference: AND HENRY MIGHT RETURN TO ENGLAND AT ANY MOMENT
records.text: and Henry might return to England at any moment.

records.reference: MARIE PICKED CHERRIES AND SANG SOFTLY TO HERSELF STRIPPING ONE GLITTERING BRANCH AFTER ANOTHER SHIVERING WHEN SHE CAUGHT A SHOWER OF RAINDROPS ON HER NECK AND HAIR
records.text: Marie picked cherries and sang softly to herself, stripping one glittering branch after another, shivering when she caught a shower of raindrops on her neck and hair.

records.reference: AT DINNER LAKE WAS EASY AND AMUSING
records.text: At dinner Lake was easy and amusing.
